name: internal-manage-system
goals: Clients read and write domain resources over HTTP.
The system notifies people through an external channel.
Metrics, structured logs and health endpoints for operations.
Files are uploaded, stored and served.
Changes are recorded append-only with the actor.
Records move in and out as files.
Large media files are stored once and played by many.
Users work in several languages and locales.

rules: strict TypeScript; no `any` in exported signatures.
No business logic in route handlers.
Every component logs one structured line per unit of work with the correlation id.
No in-process state that a second instance would not see; instances are interchangeable.
Prefer the boring option; a new piece of infrastructure needs a decision record.
Node 20 as stated in the constraints.
Stateless processes: configuration from the environment, no local files that a second instance would not see.
definition_of_done: Acceptance checks of the package pass.
No file outside the write scope changed.
Every public operation of the implemented interfaces exists with the declared inputs.

requirements.statement: Admins can create, publish and unpublish courses (videos, files, tests).
requirements.rationale: source (ja): 管理者は講座(タイトル、説明、動画ファイル、確認テスト)を作成・公開・非公開にできる。

requirements.statement: Employees can search and take courses. Employees can save and resume playback position videos later.
requirements.rationale: source (ja): 社員は講座を検索して受講し、動画の視聴位置を保存して後で再開できる。

requirements.statement: Employees can take tests. Employees can view explanations grades immediately.
requirements.rationale: no catalogue pattern matched; owner chosen by the engine (see the notes); source (ja): 社員は確認テストを受験し、採点結果と解説を即時に閲覧できる。

requirements.statement: Managers can list and view grades their reports progress. Managers can export CSV.
requirements.rationale: source (ja): 上長は部下の受講状況と成績を一覧で閲覧し、CSV でエクスポートできる。

requirements.statement: The system must notify deadline 3 days before not yet taken employees email.
requirements.rationale: source (ja): 受講期限の 3 日前に未受講の社員へメールで通知する。

requirements.statement: Courses completions grades audit for 5 years retention.
requirements.rationale: source (ja): 講座の受講完了と成績は監査のため 5 年間保持する。

requirements.statement: The system must view pages email employees locale (Japanese English).
requirements.rationale: source (ja): 画面とメールは社員のロケール(日本語・英語)で表示する。

requirements.statement: Videos files up to 2 GB. The system must complete upload within 10 min.
requirements.rationale: source (ja): 動画ファイルは最大 2GB。アップロードは 10 分以内に完了すること。

requirements.statement: The system must view videos concurrently 2000 users playback must not stall.
requirements.rationale: source (ja): 同時に 2,000 人が動画を視聴しても再生が途切れないこと。

requirements.statement: The system must respond courses list within 300 ms (p95).
requirements.rationale: source (ja): 講座一覧は 300ms 以内(p95)に応答すること。

requirements.statement: Grades must never be lost. Grades must not record double-applied.
requirements.rationale: source (ja): 成績は失われてはならず、二重に記録されてはならない。

requirements.statement: Monthly availability at least 99.9 %. The system must export Prometheus for metrics.
requirements.rationale: source (ja): 月間稼働率 99.9% 以上。Prometheus 向けメトリクスを出力する。

requirements.statement: The system can use object storage TypeScript (Node 20) PostgreSQL S3. Team of 4.
requirements.rationale: source (ja): TypeScript(Node 20)、PostgreSQL、S3 互換のオブジェクトストレージを利用可能。チームは 4 名。

requirements.statement: Employees authenticate internal SSO (OIDC). Containers existing ingress behind.
requirements.rationale: source (ja): 社員の認証は社内 SSO(OIDC)。コンテナで既存のイングレスの背後に配置する。

requirements.statement: Every operation is scoped to the caller's own resources; an admin role may act on any resource (assumed by the engine).
requirements.rationale: assumed by the engine; confirm or override

requirements.statement: The system sustains 100 requests/s with peaks of 1,000 requests/s (assumed by the engine; default, not derived from the text).
requirements.rationale: assumed by the engine; confirm or override

requirements.statement: Backups run daily with a recovery point of 24 h and a recovery time of 4 h (assumed by the engine).
requirements.rationale: assumed by the engine; confirm or override

requirements.statement: External calls time out after 10 s; failures are retried 5 times with exponential backoff and work waits durably meanwhile (assumed by the engine).
requirements.rationale: assumed by the engine; confirm or override

requirements.statement: An alert is raised when the error rate exceeds 1 % for 5 minutes or the queue depth grows for 10 minutes (assumed by the engine).
requirements.rationale: assumed by the engine; confirm or override

requirements.statement: No existing data or system to migrate from (assumed by the engine).
requirements.rationale: assumed by the engine; confirm or override

components.name: Store
components.responsibility: Owns persistence of the domain entities: durable writes, reads, listing, and the schema/migrations.

components.name: File storage
components.responsibility: Stores and serves uploaded files/blobs with content-type and size limits.

components.name: Audit log
components.responsibility: Append-only record of who did what to which resource, queryable by resource and actor.

components.name: CDN
components.responsibility: Edge cache in front of the object store; serves media by signed, expiring URLs.

components.name: Domain core
components.responsibility: Business rules and validation for the domain entities; the only module that changes state through the store.

components.name: Notifier
components.responsibility: Sends operator/customer notifications through the configured channel with templating and rate limiting.

components.name: Observability
components.responsibility: Metrics registry and exposition, structured logging, health/readiness endpoints.

components.name: Authentication
components.responsibility: Authenticates callers and resolves them to a principal and scope; enforces authorization for management operations.

components.name: Search index
components.responsibility: Full-text and filtered queries over the indexed entities.

components.name: Import/export
components.responsibility: Streams records to and from CSV/JSON with validation and partial-failure reporting.

components.name: Localisation
components.responsibility: Resolves locale, timezone and currency per request; formats messages, dates and amounts from message catalogues.

components.name: Scheduler
components.responsibility: Computes when deferred work runs next (backoff schedules, periodic jobs) and promotes due work.

components.name: Public HTTP API
components.responsibility: Translates HTTP requests into core calls: routing, request validation, error mapping, JSON.

decisions.title: API style

options.name: GraphQL
cons: complexity budget for a small team

decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), operability (weight 1.0). REST/JSON over HTTP: 1.37; gRPC: 1.25; GraphQL: 1.13
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'gRPC' gives up: typed contracts, streaming. Not choosing 'GraphQL' gives up: flexible queries.

decisions.title: Primary store
decisions.context: Domain records need durable, queryable storage.

options.name: MySQL / MariaDB (the stated database)
cons: weaker JSON and DDL ergonomics than PostgreSQL

options.name: Redis for the hot state (as stated) with a relational store for durable records
pros: the stated home of the hot data

options.name: Managed document store (DynamoDB/MongoDB, as stated)
cons: query patterns must be designed up front

decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), operability (weight 1.0). PostgreSQL: 3.37; MySQL / MariaDB: unavailable (needs mysql, not in the constraints); Redis for the hot state: unavailable (needs redis_primary, not in the constraints); Managed document store: unavailable (needs document_db, not in the constraints); SQLite: unavailable (ruled out by containers); Files: unavailable (ruled out by containers); In-memory: unavailable (ruled out by containers, postgres, durable_required). stated in the constraints

decisions.title: Caller authentication
decisions.context: Management operations must be attributable to a customer or operator.

options.name: API keys per customer, hashed at rest, sent as a bearer token
cons: no delegation or expiry unless added

options.name: OAuth2 / OIDC with the platform's identity provider
Session tokens issued by the platform's own account service to game/mobile clients (device-bound, short-lived, refreshable)
No account: a reference number plus a knowledge factor (date of birth) resumes a saved application; every attempt rate-limited and logged
pros: no credentials to manage for occasional users
cons: a reference number can be shared; scope what it unlocks

options.name: Email one-time code / magic link (no account needed)

decisions.choice: OAuth2 / OIDC with the platform's identity provider
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), operability (weight 1.0). OAuth2 / OIDC with the platform's identity provi: 2.00; API keys per customer, hashed at rest, sent as a: 1.25; Mutual TLS: 0.88; Session tokens issued by the platform's own acco: unavailable (needs game_client, not in the constraints); No account: a reference number plus a knowledge : unavailable (needs no_account_auth, not in the constraints); Email one-time code / magic link: unavailable (needs email_auth, not in the constraints). stated in the constraints
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'API keys per customer, hashed at rest, sent as a' gives up: simple, scriptable. Not choosing 'Mutual TLS' gives up: strong, no secrets in headers.

decisions.title: How media reaches viewers
decisions.context: Large files are watched by many people at once; the application must not proxy the bytes.

options.name: Object storage behind a CDN, signed expiring URLs, HTTP range requests; the application never streams bytes
pros: scales with viewers, not with instances
cons: URL signing and expiry to get right

options.name: Signed URLs straight from object storage (no CDN)
cons: latency and egress from one region

options.name: Application streams the file
cons: every viewer holds an application connection
memory and bandwidth on the instances

decisions.choice: Object storage behind a CDN, signed expiring URLs, HTTP range requests; the application never streams bytes
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), operability (weight 1.0). Object storage behind a CDN, signed expiring URL: 1.81; Signed URLs straight from object storage: 1.46; Application streams the file: 0.91
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Signed URLs straight from object storage' gives up: simplest, cheap at low volume. Not choosing 'Application streams the file' gives up: one place for authorisation.

decisions.title: Localisation approach
decisions.context: Text, dates and amounts must appear in each user's language and locale.

options.name: Message catalogues in the code base (ICU message format), locale from the user's profile then the request
Translations stored in the database and editable at runtime

decisions.choice: Message catalogues in the code base (ICU message format), locale from the user's profile then the request
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), operability (weight 1.0). Message catalogues in the code base: 1.55; Translations stored in the database and editable: 1.28
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Translations stored in the database and editable' gives up: no release for wording.

decisions.title: Concurrency control for conflicting writes
decisions.context: Two callers may change the same record at the same time and the result must be consistent.

options.name: Optimistic concurrency: version column checked on every update; conflict returns 409 and the caller retries
Row locks inside a short transaction (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE)

decisions.choice: Optimistic concurrency: version column checked on every update; conflict returns 409 and the caller retries
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), operability (weight 1.0). Optimistic concurrency: version column checked o: 1.81; Row locks inside a short transaction: 1.72; Last write wins: 1.55
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Row locks inside a short transaction' gives up: simple mental model, no client retry. Not choosing 'Last write wins' gives up: nothing to implement.

decisions.title: Redundancy for the availability target
decisions.context: The availability target must be met through instance failures and deploys.

options.name: Two or more interchangeable instances per role behind the ingress, health checks, rolling deploys
cons: needs stateless instances and a shared store

decisions.choice: Two or more interchangeable instances per role behind the ingress, health checks, rolling deploys
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), operability (weight 1.0). Two or more interchangeable instances per role b: 1.55; Active-active across two regions: 1.31; Single instance with health-based restart: 1.25
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Active-active across two regions' gives up: survives a regional outage. Not choosing 'Single instance with health-based restart' gives up: simplest, cheapest.

decisions.title: Process topology
decisions.context: The same code base serves requests and performs background work.

options.name: One image, role by flag: `api` and `worker` processes scale independently
pros: independent scaling of ingress and outbound work

options.name: Single process with background threads
cons: request latency competes with outbound work

options.name: Separate services per concern (ingest, admin, delivery)
cons: three deployables for a team of three

decisions.choice: One image, role by flag: `api` and `worker` processes scale independently
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), operability (weight 1.0). One image, role by flag: `api` and `worker` proc: 1.86; Separate services per concern: 1.43; Single process with background threads: 1.40
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Separate services per concern' gives up: clear ownership. Not choosing 'Single process with background threads' gives up: one deployable.

decisions.title: Assumed answer: load (Q-rate)
decisions.context: The requirements do not say. Question: Q-rate. No evidence in the text; engine default.
decisions.rationale: No rate stated and none derivable (a count is a size, not a rate); 100 requests/s is a modest default for a first release — every capacity figure below inherits this assumption.
decisions.consequences: If the real answer differs: State the measured or expected rate; capacity estimates and the queue decision change.

decisions.title: Assumed answer: data (Q-backup)
decisions.context: The requirements do not say. Question: Q-backup. No evidence in the text; engine default.
decisions.rationale: The store's own daily backup is the cheapest credible baseline.
decisions.consequences: If the real answer differs: State RPO/RTO; the store decision and a restore drill change.

decisions.title: Assumed answer: data (Q-migration)
decisions.context: The requirements do not say. Question: Q-migration. No evidence in the text; engine default.

decisions.title: Assumed answer: security (Q-authz)
decisions.context: The requirements do not say. Question: Q-authz. No evidence in the text; engine default.
decisions.rationale: Ownership scoping is the minimum that prevents cross-tenant access.

decisions.title: Assumed answer: resilience (Q-external)
decisions.context: The requirements do not say. Question: Q-external. No evidence in the text; engine default.
decisions.rationale: Bounded retries with a durable queue keep the system responsive during a one-hour outage.

decisions.title: Assumed answer: operations (Q-alerting)
decisions.context: The requirements do not say. Question: Q-alerting. No evidence in the text; engine default.
decisions.rationale: Two alerts catch most incidents without paging on noise.

decisions.title: Assumed answer: cost (Q-budget)
decisions.context: The requirements do not say. Question: Q-budget. No evidence in the text; engine default.

risks.description: Payloads or uploads without size limits exhaust memory or disk.
risks.mitigation: Enforce size limits at the surface; reject early with a clear error.

risks.description: Entities evolve; migrations run against live data.
risks.mitigation: Versioned migrations applied before deploy; additive changes first, removals one release later.

risks.description: A widespread failure disables many targets and emails every owner at once.
risks.mitigation: Rate-limit notifications per owner and batch them.

risks.description: Per-target labels on metrics explode cardinality.
risks.mitigation: Label by outcome and partition class, not by target id; expose per-target detail through the API instead.

risks.description: A management operation reachable without authentication.
risks.mitigation: Authenticate in one middleware for every management route; test every route unauthenticated.

risks.description: Media egress cost and bandwidth grow with viewers, not with the team's plans.
risks.mitigation: Serve through the CDN with caching headers; monitor egress per day; cap bitrate variants.

risks.description: A missing message key ships as a blank or the key itself.
risks.mitigation: Fallback to the default locale; a build check that every key exists in the default catalogue.

risks.description: Parts of the requirements were not recognised by the catalogue and received a generic decomposition.
risks.mitigation: Review the components marked generic; refine responsibilities and interfaces before briefing.
Parameterised queries only; no string-built SQL. Check: static check for string-formatted SQL finds nothing

risks.description: [information_disclosure] Store: Backups and dumps contain everything.
risks.mitigation: Encrypt backups; restrict who can take them. Check: backup file is not readable without the key

risks.description: [tampering] File storage: Uploaded content is not what its type claims.
risks.mitigation: Sniff content type; reject executables; size limits. Check: renamed executable is rejected

risks.description: [elevation] File storage: Path traversal through user-supplied names.
risks.mitigation: Generate storage keys; never use client names as paths. Check: name '../x' cannot escape the store

risks.description: [denial_of_service] Notifier: Notification storms and template injection.
risks.mitigation: Rate-limit per recipient; escape template context. Check: 1,000 failures produce one digest per owner

risks.description: [spoofing] Authentication: Credential stuffing or leaked keys.
risks.mitigation: Hash keys at rest; allow revocation; rate-limit failures. Check: revoked key is rejected within seconds; brute force is throttled

risks.description: [elevation] Authentication: A caller acts on another tenant's resources.
risks.mitigation: Every core operation takes the principal and checks ownership. Check: cross-tenant request returns 404/403 for every operation

risks.description: [spoofing] Public HTTP API: Requests without a verified caller identity reach domain operations.
risks.mitigation: Authenticate every route in one middleware; deny by default. Check: every route returns 401 without credentials

risks.description: [tampering] Public HTTP API: Malformed or oversized bodies reach the core.
risks.mitigation: Schema-validate and size-limit at the surface; reject before parsing fully. Check: fuzz the body; oversize returns 413

risks.description: [denial_of_service] Public HTTP API: A single caller saturates the service.
risks.mitigation: Per-caller rate limit and request timeouts. Check: burst from one key returns 429; others unaffected

risks.description: [information_disclosure] Public HTTP API: Stack traces or internal ids leak in error responses.
risks.mitigation: Map exceptions to fixed error shapes; log details server-side only. Check: no traceback text in any 4xx/5xx body
